full_oscillator_selector_single_phase.reference: D. A. Yarotsky, Commun. Math. Phys. 261 (2006), 799-819, Theorem 1
full_oscillator_selector_single_phase.setup: On the registered zero-source large-N corridor let P_N be the exact even/odd onsite doublet, s_N exchange its two parity eigenvectors, p_N^-=(P_N-s_N)/2, and k_N=h_site,N-epsilon_(0,N)-delta_(1,N)P_(1,N)>=Gamma_N(1-P_N). For a fixed 0<u<=1 add the bounded selector u sum_x p_(x,N)^- to the exact full-oscillator Hamiltonian. Allocate it as u[p_x^-+p_y^-]/6 on each positive cubic edge and group the three positive edges at x into the forward star Lambda_*={0,e_1,e_2,e_3}.
full_oscillator_selector_single_phase.reference_star: h_(x,N)^u=sum_(i=1)^3[(k_x+k_(x+e_i))/6+J_N(1-s_x s_(x+e_i))+u(p_x^-+p_(x+e_i)^-)/6] is classical for the product partition {p_N^+,p_N^-,high spectral projections}, has the unique kernel (Omega_N^+)^(tensor 4), and exact local gap g_(star,N)(u)=min{u,2J_N+u/6,Gamma_N/6+J_N}. For sufficiently large N with J_N>=1 this equals u.
full_oscillator_selector_single_phase.relative_form: The v1.9 edge residual estimate |V_(e,N)(psi,psi)|<=alpha_N h_(e,N)^0(psi,psi)+beta_N||psi||^2 and selector positivity give |phi_(x,N)(psi,psi)|<=alpha_N h_(x,N)^u(psi,psi)+3beta_N||psi||^2. After division by the exact gap u, Yarotsky inputs are alpha_N and 3beta_N/u.
full_oscillator_selector_single_phase.quantitative_onset: Choose witnesses C_alpha,C_beta,N_1 with alpha_N<=C_alpha N^-2, beta_N<=C_beta N^-3 and J_N>=1 for N>=N_1. If a_Y,b_Y are the existential Theorem-1 admissibility constants for dimension three and Lambda_*, then N_*(u)=max{N_1,ceil(sqrt(C_alpha/a_Y)),ceil((3C_beta/(u b_Y))^(1/3))}. Every N>=N_*(u) satisfies the theorem.
full_oscillator_selector_single_phase.conclusion: For every fixed 0<u<=1 and all sufficiently large N, the exact selected full-oscillator Hamiltonian has a nondegenerate ground vector and a positive volume-independent finite-volume spectral gap in every periodic volume, a thermodynamic weak-star ground-state limit, exponential clustering for bounded local observables, and weak-star analyticity only for parameters whose forms or resolvents are analytic inside the same admissible region. Parity gives the opposite selector theorem.
full_oscillator_selector_single_phase.boundary: The source is the bounded spectral-doublet selector, not the physical linear source. The theorem is exact on the full infinite-dimensional onsite Hilbert space but does not remove the selector, prove zero-source coexistence, identify a common real-time algebra, or prove a broken-sector GNS Hamiltonian gap. The Yarotsky constants and numerical onset are existential.

finite_full_h_continuous_core.definition: For each exact finite-volume full Q3 Hamiltonian H_Lambda put alpha_t=Ad exp(itH_Lambda/hbar) and C(H_Lambda)={A in B(H_Lambda):||alpha_t(A)-A||->0}.
finite_full_h_continuous_core.theorem: On B(H_Lambda)=M(K(H_Lambda)) the full action is bounded-strict, equivalently bounded-strong-star, continuous. C(H_Lambda) is the maximal invariant unital C-star subalgebra on which the action is point-norm C0; it contains K(H_Lambda). Every L1 temporal smear B_f=int f(s)alpha_s(B)ds lies in C(H_Lambda) and obeys ||alpha_t(B_f)-B_f||<=||B||||f(.-t)-f||_1. Smooth compactly supported smears satisfy delta(B_f)=-B_(f') and form a norm-generator core.
finite_full_h_continuous_core.energy_topology: With K_Lambda=1+H_Lambda-E_(0,Lambda), compact resolvent makes K_Lambda^-s compact. The exact action is isometric C0 for q_s(A)=||AK_Lambda^-s||+||K_Lambda^-s A||.
finite_full_h_continuous_core.kms_and_multiplier_boundary: Every finite Gibbs state restricts to a beta-KMS state on C(H_Lambda). Combined with R-167 v2.8, C(H_Lambda) intersects the bounded continuous configuration multipliers exactly in C times the identity.

all_finite_uniform_continuous_product.definition: In M=product_Lambda B(H_Lambda), with diagonal exact actions, C_u consists of bounded families A such that sup_Lambda||alpha_t^Lambda(A_Lambda)-A_Lambda|| tends to zero.
all_finite_uniform_continuous_product.theorem: C_u is the maximal invariant unital C-star subalgebra carrying the diagonal point-norm C0 action and is the norm closure of coordinatewise L1 temporal smears. Each coordinate evaluation is a surjective equivariant quotient C_u->C(H_Lambda), and the smooth generators intertwine. The existing universal L1 orbit-smear carrier embeds equivariantly. At fixed beta, finite Gibbs evaluation states and all of their weak-star cluster points are beta-KMS on C_u.
all_finite_uniform_continuous_product.boundary: C_u is categorical and beta/state independent, but it has no spatial net, no exhaustion-identification relation, and no claim that a single local seed has Cauchy images across shapes.

fixed_beta_os_mixture_continuous_core.definition: For the previously reconstructed fixed-beta mixture W-star system (M_beta,alpha^beta,psi_+,psi_-), let A_(beta,c)={X:||alpha_t^beta(X)-X||->0}.
fixed_beta_os_mixture_continuous_core.theorem: A_(beta,c) is the weak-star dense maximal invariant norm-C0 C-star subalgebra of M_beta. Smooth temporal smears are a generator core. The two normal beta-KMS phase states restrict to distinct beta-KMS states: if B distinguishes them and int f=1, invariance gives psi_+(B_f)-psi_-(B_f)=psi_+(B)-psi_-(B).
fixed_beta_os_mixture_continuous_core.boundary: This is fixed-beta and phase-pair derived. It does not identify exact finite Hamiltonian exhaustions with the OS mixture, construct a beta-independent spatial quasi-local algebra, or select a ground state.

selector_add_subtract_no_go.fixture: Put the selector in the reference and subtract it in the perturbation to recover the zero-source Hamiltonian. On the all-minus forward-star vector the reference expectation is u and the counterselector expectation is -u, so the normalized relative ratio is exactly one for every N and u. Also 3beta_N/u diverges at fixed N as u tends to zero.
selector_add_subtract_no_go.scope: This rejects only automatic selector removal through the same one-phase small-relative-form theorem. It is not a no-go for zero-source phases by a genuine two-phase method.

n_dependent_radius_no_go.fixture: Let theta_N=N^-3 be a defect and r_N=N^-4 the positive theorem radius. Both tend to zero, but theta_N>r_N for every N>=2.
n_dependent_radius_no_go.scope: Vanishing oscillator defects plus a separately existential positive radius for each N do not imply eventual two-phase theorem entry. A common positive lower radius or a quantitative comparison is required. This grants the doublet reference and is distinct from the earlier classical-minima direct-import mismatch.

categorical_exhaustion_no_go.fixture: On M2 take H_(2m)=0, H_(2m+1)=diag(0,1), and A_n=sigma_x. The generators are uniformly bounded, so A belongs to C_u. At t=pi/2 the evolved observables alternate between sigma_x and sigma_y and have distance sqrt(2). At beta=log 2, the Gibbs expectation of E_22 alternates between 1/2 and 1/3; the odd KMS oracle is omega(E_12 alpha_(i beta)(E_21))=1/3=omega(E_21 E_12).
categorical_exhaustion_no_go.scope: This rejects only the implication from categorical C0/KMS compactness to all-shape Cauchy convergence or a unique phase quotient. It is not a Q3 thermodynamic nonexistence theorem.
